security_findings.evidence: E6Y local catalog and E6O rollback-only correction
security_findings.scope: public.write_audit_event and public.enqueue_notification currently SQL EXECUTE-granted to anon/authenticated
security_findings.proposed_action: Review existing source-only REVOKE migration in parity staging; do not deploy yet
security_findings.impact_risk: Audit integrity, queue continuity, trusted nested caller rights

security_findings.evidence: E6Y default privileges: two client-role EXECUTE grants for future postgres-created public functions
security_findings.scope: Future functions, not existing function grants
security_findings.proposed_action: Decide allowlisted explicit RPC grants and owner/schema-specific ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES plan on separately approved stage
security_findings.impact_risk: Breaking valid public discovery/registration RPCs and exposing new internal functions

security_findings.evidence: E6Y default privileges: sixteen table privilege entries including TRUNCATE to anon and authenticated
security_findings.scope: Future postgres-created public tables; TRUNCATE is not subject to row-level security
security_findings.proposed_action: Assess necessary table grants including TRUNCATE separately; require allowlisted stage changes and rollback
security_findings.impact_risk: Future whole-table operations and privileged data pathways; RLS does not protect TRUNCATE

security_findings.evidence: E6Y default privileges: six sequence privilege entries for anon/authenticated
security_findings.scope: Future postgres-created public sequences, not necessarily REST exposed
security_findings.proposed_action: Determine legitimate USAGE/SELECT/UPDATE requirements before proposing restricted default grant
security_findings.impact_risk: Generated IDs, insert workflow and sequence predictability/availability

security_findings.evidence: E6Y 13 non-trigger SQL EXECUTE candidates under checked-in public API schema
security_findings.scope: Potential review candidates, not demonstrated reachable routes or exploitation
security_findings.proposed_action: Independently inspect deployed PostgREST schema/config, exact arg/default mapping and authorised GoTrue calls
security_findings.impact_risk: Misclassification of direct RPC reachability, mistaken authentication/authorisation assumptions

security_findings.evidence: E6S privacy proposal and E6R role metadata callsites
security_findings.scope: Role/helper disclosure contract; provider-public columns and technical helper controls
security_findings.proposed_action: Obtain independently signed D1-D5 policy choices before proposing migration
security_findings.impact_risk: Cross-person role exposure and broken legitimate scoped workflows

prerequisites.meaning: Exact dedicated stage and test scope authorised by product owner
Verified restore, baseline checksum and isolated rollback plan
Real owner/ACL/RLS/default privilege/schema parity and independent diff review
Independent actual identity negative/positive HTTP PostgREST traces
Authenticated service audit, notification enqueue, outbox delivery/cleanup
Human data minimisation and cross-person disclosure decisions
Independent Security and Operations plus DR/Privacy as required
Formal independent program gates remain unsigned

constraints: No shared database migrations or ACL changes
No auto sign-offs or enabling E7+
No changes to paused T2.4 code or services
No PostgREST production requests or real identities
No private catalogues, passwords or user data in GitHub
Scope applies only to Wantok Services, never GVE
